tldr: On Oct 14 a paper proposed Lifted State Policy Optimization to credit the local change that turns a flawed reasoning state into a better one. On Oct 22 ReflectPO applied reflection-guided policy optimization to long-horizon LLM agents.
whats_new: SOPO (Oct 23) applies Socratic guided policy optimization to span-level hallucination detection in LLM output.
why_it_matters: Three arXiv papers in ten days tailor policy optimization to self-correction, agent horizons and hallucination detection; all are preprints, so treat them as research signals, not production tooling.

beats.headline: Lifted State Policy Optimization targets self-correction
ReflectPO brings reflection-guided optimization to long-horizon agents
SOPO aims policy optimization at span-level hallucination detection

open_questions: Do any of these three methods publish code or reproducible results on public benchmarks?
take_for_builders: Treat these as preprints: wait for released code and independent replication before changing any training or eval pipeline.

day_captions.a42e86ea9f9f98f3: Introduces Lifted State Policy Optimization, crediting the local change from a flawed reasoning state to a better one.
day_captions.9cbcaf295333969d: Extends policy optimization with reflection guidance for long-horizon, tool-using LLM agents.
day_captions.78e0961a0062764b: Uses Socratic guided policy optimization to detect hallucinated spans rather than whole answers.
